Which brings me to the most important point not only in your message but anyone's lives:

Never felt happy

Happiness is the only thing that matters and it really only depends on how you handle your life. I'm not talking about "fake it til you make it' or "be positive" crap. Not only happiness is confused with joy far too often, it ought not to be a noun at all. Happiness is a verb, it's an activity, it's the art of living day-to-day while being true to yourself - not who other people want you to be or who you think you should be but who you really are. There is no grander achievement in life or harder task because self-knowledge is also an unending activity. You're healthy, free and sane - there is nothing preventing you from being happy except yourself.

A lot of people like to go to therapists and find that it really helps them in this task. There is no shame in that, if you do so though (and do not do it already), you could try - just remember not to settle with a therapist just because someone indicated you. Make your first encounter a triage, if you don't come out with a "this is it" feeling from this session look for someone else. Also, one year is good enough time for therapy - if you get to that point and isn't satisfied it's time to look for someone else.

Myself, I like to study philosophy, ethics and do a lot of introversion. I don't feel like a therapist helps me much and I've tried due to other people asking me to do it - it just goes nowhere with me. There is a ton of material about what is happiness and once you understand it, you can figure out what it means for you and how to figure it on your own life. As with therapy, philosophy is not for everyone either but one of many paths to happiness.
